correctness.rationale: All quantifiers n>=3 and semisimplicial face conventions are fixed. The cyclic subcomplexes are CW pushouts of simplices with a disconnected two-component first overlap and contractible later overlaps. Their intersection is the n(n-1)-edge complete bidirected graph. Integer cocycles c_plus(uv)=[u>v] and c_minus(uv)=[u<v] evaluate on a digon and a directed triangle as (1,1) and (1,2), determinant 1. Van Kampen kills both circle generators and integral Mayer-Vietoris gives free second homology of rank (n-1)^2-2 with no other reduced homology; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the unrestricted wedge of S^2. Standalone modular computations for n=3..8 and exact intersection identities support but do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: A naturally defined infinite family formed by all dihedral rotations has a complete nonequivariant homotopy type, while each orientation alone retains a circle. The precise primitive two-winding mechanism explains how combining the orientations kills the circle and creates quadratically many integral two-spheres, a stronger and structurally useful fact than a free fundamental group or an Euler-characteristic count. This provides an explicit benchmark for ordered-word topology; no unsupported all-permutation or equivariant classification is claimed.
